chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the pre-dawn meal (suhur) for the one who intends to fast, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for during the month of Ramadan, then there is merit in the pre-dawn meal, even if it is by drinking a sip of water; and as for voluntary fasting, whoever wishes to take the pre-dawn meal, let him do so, and whoever does not do so, there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the pre-dawn meal (suhur) before fasting in Ramadan versus voluntary fasts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the obligatory nature of suhur in Ramadan, where even a sip of water carries spiritual merit, and its optional status for voluntary fasts. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maximizing reward through minimal effort in Ramadan, while maintaining flexibility for nafl fasting. The ruling underscores the prophetic tradition of starting the day with sustenance to strengthen worship.
